newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols under pressure after PPI.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols under pressure after PPI.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options sagged in Friday's shortened session after bonds rallied on weak economic data and concern set in about time-decay over a long weekend, dealers said.
"Volatilities got whacked after the PPI (producer price index) numbers," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.

Implied volatility for CBOT March T-bond futures options, which expire next Friday, tumbled to about 6.5 percent from Thursday's 8.2 percent close. April and June were off 0.1-0.2 points each to around 9.0 and 9.5 percent respectively.

Traders said a raft of soft economic data this week, coming on the heels of a benign January employment report last week, convinced the market that the Federal Reserve would keep interest rates steady for a while.

Overall U.S. PPI fell 0.3 percent in January against an average Wall Street estimate of a 0.3 percent rise and after a revised 0.6 percent climb in December. The core PPI, excluding food and energy prices, was unchanged in January after a 0.1 percent rise in December.
The numbers sent March T-bond futures to a high of 114-3/32, just short of the December 30 high at 114-6/32.

But traders warned that the bond market could be running out of steam, at least in the near term, noting that open interest in T-bond futures had grown to record levels -- 560,280 at Thursday's close -- during the recent rally.
The brokerage trader said bonds, which pulled back slightly after the initial rally on PPI, seemed to lack resilience when weak industrial production data came in later in the morning.
"There's just nobody left to buy it up," he said. "What it tells me is that the market is really overbought and people aren't going to buy on just mediocre weakness."
Industrial production in January was unchanged after rising a revised 0.5 percent rise in December.
By late morning, traders said options trading was grinding to a halt. CBOT financial products close early today at 1210 CST/1810 GMT and will be shut on Monday for the Presidents' Day holiday.
The shorter end of the yield curve was also very quiet, with volatilities for Eurodollar futures options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange narrowly lower.
Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollars were off 0.1 0.2 point at 8.7 and 12.2 percent, respectively.
With front-month Eurodollar futures stagnating amid a steady interest rate outlook, shorter-dated options were particularly under pressure because of their steeper time decay, traders said.
CME interest rate products close today at 1200 CST/1800 GMT and will be shut on Monday.
